messages:
maria: Quick idea for sticky-key routing + quota-handoff window. Instead of immediate fallbacks, keep a short affinity window (e.g., 30s) where requests from the same API key try to stick to project quota before moving to org quota. Could reduce oscillation for spiky clients.

devon: interesting. Does sticky affinity mean we reserve tokens in project counter for the window? Concern: reservation leaks if client disappears mid-window.

maria: not reserving long-term. Plan: optimistic local lease (ephemeral token balance) on the edge node for X seconds. Edge decrements local lease then asynchronously reconciles with central counters. If reconciliation fails, we emit a charge-correction event.

ravi: left to implement: conflict resolution on async reconciliation. If central says "overdrawn", we could either issue a compensating debit (negative event) or throttle next request. Prefered: produce a correction event to metrics + sample the offending request for replay.

ella: console POV: owners want "affinity heat" so they can see which keys repeatedly hit handoffs. Also a timeline of reconciliation errors.

maria: sample policy YAML: 

```yaml
quota_policy: sticky_handoff
affinity_window_seconds: 30
edge_lease: true
async_reconcile: true
reconcile_strategy: charge_correction
reconcile_max_delay_ms: 200
telemetry: 
  - name: affinity_event
    fields: [key_id, project_id, org_id, node_id, event_type, tokens, lease_ttl]
  - name: reconcile_outcome
    fields: [key_id, outcome, delta_tokens, sample_request_id]
```

ravi: for low-latency we should avoid a sync roundtrip to central counters on every request. Memcache-style lease + kafka reconciler seems fine. But we need circuit breaker if reconciler backlog grows.

maria: agreed. Circuit breaker rules: if reconcile backlog > 100k events or reconcile-rate drops, disable edge leases for the affected region and fall back to synchronous project->org check. Emit alert to #eng-oncall.

devon: auth nuance: this interacts with service-account impersonation. If a request uses an impersonation token, which quota do we attribute? The calling key or the impersonated project? We should keep existing rule: attribute to the effective origin project (impersonated) but record caller key as provenance.

ella: console UX: show both attribution columns: attributed_project (billing) and provenance_key (owner). Add quick filter: show incidents where these differ.

ops-bot: reconcile-processor deployed to staging at 2026-02-15T09:40:12Z.

ravi: rollout plan: feature-flagged per-region. Start with read-only edge lease (doesn't decrement central counters) for 48h to gather telemetry. Then enable write-mode for 1% of orgs for 24h, monitor negative-corrections, then ramp.

maria: alerting: create prometheus gauges: reconcile_queue_size, correction_rate_per_min, affinity_handovers_per_min. Also a high-cardinality kafka topic for sampled reconcile events.

devon: one more: billing implications. If we do charge_correction, downstream billing needs stable ordering. Suggest batch corrections once/day to billing to avoid invoice churn. Console shows provisional vs settled usage.

maria: good catch. We'll tag events provisional=true until settled in nightly job. Console should show provisional badge and link to settled ledger.

ella: ok. I'll mock console panels: affinity heatmap, reconciliation timeline, provisional vs settled usage toggle, and a per-key replay link.

ravi: impl tasks: 1) edge lease library (language bindings), 2) reconcile processor + backlog monitor, 3) billing settle pipeline update, 4) console mockups, 5) runbook for disabling leases.

maria: I'll file RFC with these tasks and attach proto schemas for telemetry. If anyone has blockers speak now.

devon: none from me. schedule PO for billing signoff.

maria: thanks all. If we see excessive correction_rate in canary, we'll flip feature flag off and revert to strong synchronous checks. :thumbsup:
